Left Behind

Sep 2025: Analysis

Purpose

This is a pilot study that is intended to further explore the feeling of being left behind. Specifically, we wanted to see what people intuitively write when prompted to think of the ways in which they are being left behind. Potentially, the extent to which they feel left behind, interacted with the way in which they are left behind, inform important political outcomes.

Procedure

Demographics

Demographic information, political ideology, and political party identification.

Left behind

Continuous measure

They indicated the extent to which they feel left behind on a scale of 0-100.

Open-ended measure

They wrote, in detail, what feeling left behind means to them and what are the factors that are contributing to that feeling.

Dimensions of feeling behind

They rated their response on a number of follow-up measures: systemic-individual; relation to government; economic-cultural; historic-recent; trajectory.

Outcomes

Random order: (1) support for anti-democratic practices; (2) ideal candidate for an election;
Random order: (3) anti-establishment sentiment; (4) trust in institutions.

Finally, participants indicated their voting behavior in 2024.

Eligibility

There was on bot-check with an invisible attention check.

eligible_n <- df_lebe %>% 
  group_by(is_elg) %>% 
  summarise(n = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(is_elg == 1) %>% 
  select(n) %>% 
  unlist() %>% 
  unname()

df_lebe %>% 
  group_by(att_1) %>% 
  summarise(N = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(Perc = round(100*(N/sum(N)),2)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  kbl() %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover",
                full_width = F,
                position = "left")
att_1 N Perc
1 198 100

That gives us a total of 198 eligible participants.

Participants were recruited through Prolific and the following quota was set for political representativeness: (30% dems; 30% reps; 40% independents)

Politics

Ideology

Participants were asked about the extent to which they subscribe to the following ideologies on a scale of 1-7 (select NA if unfamiliar): Conservatism, Liberalism, Democratic Socialism, Libertarianism, Progressivism.

means <- df_lebe_elg %>%
  dplyr::select(PID,ideo_con:ideo_prog) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-PID,
               names_to = "ideo",
               values_to = "score") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(score)) %>% 
  group_by(ideo) %>% 
  summarise(score = mean(score)) %>% 
  ungroup()

df_lebe_elg %>%
  dplyr::select(PID,ideo_con:ideo_prog) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-PID,
               names_to = "ideo",
               values_to = "score") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(score)) %>%  
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(aes(x = score), fill = "lightblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1,7),
                     breaks = seq(1,7,1)) +
  geom_vline(data = means,mapping = aes(xintercept = score),
             color = "black",
             linetype = "dashed",
             size = 1.1) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "grey66"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold")) +
  facet_wrap(~ideo,nrow = 2)

Measures

Left behind

Continuous

People in America come from all walks of life. Some feel left behind. We are interested in whether you feel left behind and what that means for you.

To what extent do you feel left behind? (0 = Not at All Left Behind to 100 = Extremely Left Behind)

df_lebe_elg %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = lebe_cont)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "lightblue",
                 binwidth = 10) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,100,20),
                     limits = c(-10,110)) +
  ylab("count") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(df_lebe_elg$lebe_cont,na.rm = T),
             color = "black",
             linetype = "dashed",
             size = 1.1) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "grey66"),

        axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(color = "black",

Open-ended description

[For those under 50 in the continuous measure:

Although not everyone might feel overall left behind to the same extent, everyone likely does feel left behind in at least a few ways. So, regardless of your answer to the previous question…]

What does the phrase ‘feeling left behind’ mean to you in your own life? In what ways[,if any,] do you feel left behind, and why?

Please describe why you might feel left behind in as much detail as possible. There is no right or wrong answer here; just your honest thoughts about the factors that might make you feel left behind.

paste disabled
character range: 100-5000

Note: Adding their self-reported left-behind scores to the table below as well.

I am a caucasian appearing, white, straight, Christian. I vaguely remember the first time my personality was ascribed to as being “nerdy” when really I was obsessive. I’ve been seen as cool at times, but even that is fake. Honestly what is left behind most in me is what I identify with most which is objective truth. Times and seasons come and go but the truth of the moment is always the truth, and I find since I cling to it, I am always in some way shape or form left behind. I am in a current situation where out of no where my anxiety got so bad that I can’t really do anything. I can’t see a doctor to find out what it is. I need a doctors analysis before I can get “disability”. Without income, I can’t try to attempt to heal myself. So, every door is closed. Every single one. I can’t even talk to anyone on the phone. One person tried to talk to me, but she was married, from another continent, and ultimately her mind could not even cope with the suffering I was experiencing so she ascribed ill-intent rather than understanding the objective truth of the matter. So, now I am without no one, no money, no one understands. I am completely, objectively, left behind. No one is more left behind than me, maybe other than a dead person. It sounds so far fetched what I am saying that most would think it’s a lie. Even I think it’s a lie, just because the truth is so painful. Because everyone is so busy wearing victimhood as a fashion statement to get attention, real victims are unseen, uncared about, etc. The world is exhausted with caring. And that’s fine. I just desire the truth to be known, regardless. It’s not me that’s left behind really, it’s the truth, and I think I have diagnosed the culprit of my illness in that. The body keeps score, they say, and I cannot visualize/imagine myself being healthy in a world that feels like an atmosphere of lies. It is like an invisible toxic wasteland that only reflections of lies and evil can coexist with. So maybe I am not sick at all, maybe reality is sick and I am like a fish in poisoned water trying to figure out why I am not well. I’m utterly left behind as a truth lover in a society where lies are God.
80 I have been left behind because of financial instability. Even as a person who did not finish college, I should have more opportunities than I do. Being left behind, to me, means that I am not offered the opportunities that others in my peer group have been.
35 Both due to choices I have made, such as being a stay at home parent, or choices out of my control, like suffering from chronic health conditions, I at times feel further behind because my life looks different than my peers. However, I am comparing situations often without having all of the details. As a society we elevate certain lifestyles over others, but the reality is most of us are trying our best and doing what we have to. Does my life look like I imagined it would at 37. It doesn’t but that does not mean I have been left behind. I just means my life is different.
90 because current policies and politics are being enacted that would do great harm to someone such as myself. The programs which would help me are being dismantled or are more difficult to get onto now
20 I would say having that feeling that other people are moving ahead in life in terms of career, relationships, or growth, while personally I feel somehow stuck or moving slower. At a personal level, I view it where my peers have achieved milestones such as buying a house, travelling, among other things in life. Feeling left behind always comes as a result of comparison with friends. At that moment I feel my growth, healing or journey is always lagging behind..
60 I am 54 and I was recently diagnosed auhd. I feel that had i had a diagnosis long ago my outcome would have been better or I would have had more support.
19 Struggling financially and living in poverty. Drowning in debts and not being able to pay them and not making enough money to live comfortably
80 I feel left behind in the sense that other in life have it easier to make more money and move up the corporate ladder due to their race of being Caucasian. Other minorities are being held back due to systemic racism in America and it seem’s to be getting worse by the day.
28 It means, have you been able to achieve what people of your age or education status have achieved in their lives
51 So feeling left behind for me. It’s pretty hard sometimes being stuck in a low end job where I’m basically scraping by to me. It means watching everyone else move ahead friends from school buying houses traveling or getting promotions while I’m still in the same right barely making rent. I feel left behind because it seems like I missed some boat you know maybe it’s not having gone to college or not taking risk when I was younger and now the gap is just growing the paycheck barely covers bills and seeing others post about their fancy vacations or new cars on social media stings it’s like they’re living a life. I can’t even dream of reaching plus the job itself doesn’t offer much chance to move up so I’m stuck watching time pass while others build something better.
90 As a professional writer I was making $250 an hour. Then AI happened and it ruined my career. America doesn’t care. I was just a cog in the machine and I’ve been replaced.
44 Left behind could mean that the people around you such as friends, family members and neighbors are progressing in life further than you.
14 I feel left behind in the sense that I do not communicate with anyone from grade-school while most of the other friends in the groups I was a part of have strong relationships with one another. I also feel left behind because people my age have kids that are much older than mine and they seem more financially stable.
76 for me the above phrase means that whatever i want in life i cannot achieve because of some factors . this factors might be avoidable or unavoidable. this may be in factors such as career, marriage or relationship where my peers are advancing while am still stuck at a certain level, where i might be struggling or even no change at all.
20 Being ignored by people in power, who have the ability to help people that deserve a hand. A lot of people are struggling these days because they have been left behind at the expense of the richest people in society
25 I feel like being left behind in this case means the government doesn’t care about you and not helping you in any way through policy. This makes you feel like you are getting further behind in life.
0 Feeling left behind means seeing others progress while feeling you are stuck, often due to comparism and external pressure. It can be discouraging but also motivating if the energy is chanelled possitively
21 There is so many ways you might feel left behind, like career progression, you might feel left behind if your peers are achieving promotions, higher salaries,or more prestigious role while you feel stagnant in your own career. You might also feel left behind if friends are getting married and starting a family.
70 To me it means being able to accomplish things in life. I feel like the generation I’m in keeps experiencing traumatic events and are somewhat behind in life.
61 I made some bad choices early in my life-17 to be exact, that left a profound effect on the rest of my life. I was a very intelligent, involved student throughout school. However, due to family financial issues and my choices, life took a much different direction than what I had envisioned when I was younger. My mother committed suicide when I was just 13 and that was a major turning point for me. Between that and my choice to have sex at 17 which resulted in me getting pregnant, my dream of going in the navy and later studying oceanography vanished. It was 1977, RvW was a big thing then. My dad wanted me to have the abortion, my stepmom wanted me to have the baby and keep it. Nobody asked what I wanted, so I decided. I had the baby and put him up for adoption. So, I was left behind. I was not able to pursue my career choice, I had to settle and make the best of it.
90 I am not merely speaking for myself, but what most Americans face - stagnant wages, rising costs, economic uncertainty, a government that works to line the pockets of capitalists and oligarchs and to crush its opponents
17 Feeling left behind to me would mean my family not including me when it comes to certain events. I want to be involved with all decisions and be included.
0 I think feeling left behind would mean that I feel disconnected from other people and the world around me overall. I would feel isolated and alone if I felt left behind in my life. If I feel left behind in my life, I would feel like I have no one to turn to in times of need.
94 Mainly it is about not being able to afford the things I used to or should be able to since I have a job. It’s financially being left behind by inflation.
10 For me, feeling left behind means watching others and my peers move forward in their careers or personal lives while I feel stuck in the same place. But I now recognize that I am just being too critical of myself and learned to focus on my own progress.
0 feeling left behind means seeing others reach a milestone in life while i feel stuck in the same place or slower in comparism
3 Due to my African-American race and living in the USA the phrase “left behind” generally makes me think of the mental, physical and financial constraints that slavery gifted my people with. I personally have lived my life refusing to be a continued slave. Using the excuse of being held down or “left behind” by harboring the attitude that society owes me. Is making your own pity party. That without a societal apology for our enslavement or financial blessing I can’t achieve. Yes it would be nice to have reparations for the cruelty my race suffered. I feel one must make a choice to not be or feel “left behind”. I made that choice and have never looked back. I educated myself and made a good life for myself. I overcame many obstacles but I pushed through. Left Behind will never be me or my children’s life status.
31 I sometimes feel left behind financially, because despite working hard, I struggle to build savings, pay off debt, or afford major life milestones. Others around me are advancing - earning more, investing, or reaching financial goals - while I feel stuck just trying to stay afloat. It’s frustrating and discouraging to compare myself to peers who appear financially secure, especially when I’ve faced setbacks. I sometimes feel ashamed, anxious about the future, and uncertain of whether I’ll ever catch up.
20 I’d say rising costs, rapid change, and weak safety nets make it hard to keep pace despite effort.
58 I feel t could mean many things. I could mean that your are far behind your peers in terms of success, like buying a house or getting married. Or for a child that could mean being behind academically
50 The main way I feel left behind is based on age. I have extensive administrative experience but because of my age, it is difficult to find work in a corporate setting. Companies are more geared to hiring young people without experience who are willing to work for little pay so that they do have the cost associated with high quality experience. This has led me to do other work outside of the corporate structure.
61 I live in the UP of Michigan which is an extremely rural place we dont even have Doordash pr Uber, we only have a Burger King within a half hour drive I feel like Im left behind in eerything thats new and current. A social life, concerts, more schooling. Just the hustle and bustle of city life. Political protests standing up for things I believe in.
70 I think that the social structure in the U.S allows for a wide variety of cracks to fall through. I’ve personally felt left behind in the sense that it has felt impossible to provide entirely for myself even as my income has increased. The requirements to gain that income (College, etc) place weights of debt around the shoulders of anyone without a family who can afford to pay for them.
22 I would say left behind means you have no way of taking care of yourself and no one to help you including the government. Possibly no living or food assistance and you are almost if not homeless. I do not feel this way but i understand those who do.

Dimensions of feeling left behind

Systemic-Individual


Would you say the factors that make you feel left behind are more systemic (larger forces outside your control, like government, society, culture, or the economy) or more individual (your own circumstances and choices)? (1 = Entirely Systemic to 7 = Entirely Individual)

*Note: I reverse-scored it here so it’s more intuitive for us.

df_lebe_elg %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = system_R)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "lightblue",
                 binwidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1,7,1),
                     limits = c(0,8)) +
  ylab("count") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(df_lebe_elg$system_R,na.rm = T),
             color = "black",
             linetype = "dashed",
             size = 1.1) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "grey66"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold"))

Support for anti-democratic practices

Broken up:

means <- df_lebe_elg %>%
  dplyr::select(PID,trust_con:trust_news) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-PID,
               names_to = "inst",
               values_to = "trust") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(trust)) %>% 
  group_by(inst) %>% 
  summarise(score = mean(trust)) %>% 
  ungroup()

df_lebe_elg %>%
  dplyr::select(PID,trust_con:trust_news) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-PID,
               names_to = "inst",
               values_to = "trust") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(trust)) %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x = trust)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "lightblue",
                 binwidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1,4,1),
                     limits = c(0,5)) +
  ylab("count") +
  geom_vline(data = means,mapping = aes(xintercept = score),
             color = "black",
             linetype = "dashed",
             size = 1.1) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "grey66"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold")) +
  facet_wrap(~inst,nrow = 2)

Analysis

Correlations

To explore these correlations and more, see here:

Shiny App: Correlations

Interactions

There are a bunch of ways to interact these variables. Feel free to explore here:

Shiny App: Interactions

Note that these are just raw interactions, without controlling for main effects or any other variables. Let’s start adding controls in the following linear models.

Linear models

Ok, now to run some actual stats. We want to see if these correlations and interactions hold when controlling for some important variables. I’ll show a few of them below, but if you want to try some yourself, feel free to explore here:

Shiny App: Linear Models

DV: Candidate support for sweeping-incremental change

Just as a reminder, this is the measure for this DV…

Thinking about how they would approach change, what approach would you like them to take?
1 = Sweeping (bold, radical changes); 7 = Incremental (smaller, step-by-step changes)

Model 1


Outcome: Incremental change candidate
Predictor: left behind - continuous
Controls: political ideology (conservatism), party ID, age, income, education, race, gender

m1 <- lm(elect_change ~ lebe_cont + ideo_con + party_gen + age + income_num + edu_num + race + gender,data = df_lebe_elg)
